reference: Parity cases run the same bounded shell fixture with system Bash resolving GNU Coreutils mkdir from /usr/bin and with bash-os resolving its mkdir builtin on an empty PATH. GNU exit behavior is checked by explicit per-command status capture in the script; the harness compares script status, stdout bytes, and resulting fixture tree including modes. The metadata contract uses Bash's documented type and help builtins and has no GNU CLI oracle.
coverage: multiple ordinary operands, a spaced name, and a trailing slash
nested -p creation and idempotent repetition of existing directories
default modes under a fixed umask for direct and intermediate directories
explicit modes with -m and preservation of an existing parent during mkdir -p
-- option termination for a directory name beginning with a dash
missing operand and existing-directory errors with captured statuses
failure at a non-directory path component while independent operands are still created
Bash builtin type and short-help metadata contract
exclusions: symbolic mode edge cases, unusual filesystem errors, and concurrent creation races are not covered

cases.purpose: Create multiple ordinary operands, including a name containing spaces and a valid trailing slash, then compare the resulting entries.
Create nested parents with -p, then repeat existing targets and add a sibling beneath an existing parent.
Check that ordinary and recursively created directory permissions reflect the fixed umask.
Apply explicit modes to a direct target and the final -p target while preserving the mode of a pre-existing ancestor.
cases.script:
umask 077
mkdir -p protected
umask 022
mkdir -p -m 0711 protected/branch/leaf
mkdir -m 0640 explicit

cases.purpose: Use -- to create a relative directory whose name begins with a dash.
Check the nonzero status and diagnostic for a call with no directory operand. Diagnostic prefixes and help hints are implementation-specific; status and presence of the error are the contract.
cases.script:
if mkdir; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check that creating an existing directory without -p fails and leaves it present.
cases.script:
mkdir target
if mkdir target; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 70
[[ -d target ]] || exit 71
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: A regular file blocks one operand; check its failure status and that mkdir still creates the independent operands before and after it.
cases.script:
printf x > blocker
if mkdir before blocker/child after; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 70
[[ -d before && -d after && ! -e blocker/child ]] || exit 71
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Verify through Bash builtins that mkdir resolves as a builtin and has short help metadata; no external command is used and this is not GNU CLI parity.
Explicit directory modes and existing directory preservation match GNU mkdir.
Explicit directory modes and existing directory preservation match GNU mkdir.
cases.script: mkdir -m 700 existing; mkdir -p -m 755 existing; stat -c %a existing

cases.purpose: Explicit directory modes and existing directory preservation match GNU mkdir.
cases.script: umask 077; mkdir -p -m 755 parent/final; stat -c %a parent parent/final

cases.purpose: Compare symbolic final modes and intermediate permissions under a restrictive umask.
cases.script:
umask 077
mkdir -m u=rwx,g=rx,o= symbolic
mkdir -p -m a=rx deep/leaf

cases.purpose: Follow an existing relative symlink parent and preserve its target and idempotent child.
cases.script:
mkdir real
ln -s real alias
mkdir -p alias/child
mkdir -p alias/child

cases.purpose: Reject an invalid symbolic mode without creating the target.
